sections.label: Contact address filing mandate
sections.summary: The Bill mandates filing a contact address with the Registrar, which will be made public instead of the residential address.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To improve the protection of residential addresses filed with the Registrar, the Bill will mandate the filing of a contact address, alongside the residential address.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: With this, the Registrar will make public the contact address and not the residential address.

sections.label: Contact address made public
sections.summary: The alternate contact address will be made public instead of the residential address, and providing it is required with no payment needed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This alternate address will be made public, instead of the residential address.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: However, under the new contact address regime, the provision of a contact address is required and there will be no need for payment.

sections.label: Registrar collecting additional information
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Registrar to collect additional information like email addresses and mobile numbers for secure digital communications through BizFile.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower the Registrar to collect additional information, such as email addresses and mobile numbers, to enable ACRA to send secure digital communications through BizFile, which is ACRA's business registration and filing portal.

sections.label: Documents through digital mailbox
sections.summary: The Bill empowers the Registrar to send documents and information, other than Court summonses, through the digital mailbox.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill will empower the Registrar to send documents and information, other than Court summonses, through the digital mailbox.

sections.label: Clarify deemed receipt of documents
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can clarify how documents will be deemed to have been received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how documents will be deemed to have been received?

sections.label: Clarify disclosing residential address
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can clarify how publicly disclosing an individual's residential address assists in obtaining the individual's response or notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how publicly disclosing an individual's residential address will assist in obtaining the individual's response or bringing any document to the individual's notice?

sections.label: ACRA third party data protection
sections.summary: The Minister is asked how ACRA will ensure personal data given to third parties is protected and not reused for marketing or sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share how ACRA will ensure that information, especially personal data, provided to third parties will be adequately protected and not be subsequently used by these third parties for other purposes, such as marketing or sales?

sections.label: Clause 8 information powers
sections.summary: Clause 8 empowers the Registrar or Authority to obtain information from specified sources, including Government agencies, to ascertain registration veracity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Clause 8 empowers the Registrar or Authority to obtain information related to ascertaining the veracity of registration from certain specified sources, including Government agencies.

sections.label: Doing Business ranking
sections.summary: The World Bank's most recent Doing Business Report ranked the nation second overall and fourth on Starting a Business, behind New Zealand, Georgia and Canada.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The most recent edition of the World Bank's Doing Business Report ranked our nation second overall in terms of ease of doing business.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Even so, the Starting a Business sub-indicator, the one that is most related to the Bill at hand, held us at fourth, behind New Zealand, Georgia and Canada.

sections.label: Residential address exclusion
sections.summary: New sections 30C and 30D allow residential addresses to be excluded from public disclosure if contact addresses are also available.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, the new section 30C and 30D affords the exclusion of residential addresses from public disclosure, so long as contact addresses are also available.

sections.label: World Bank indicator suspension
sections.summary: The World Bank suspended publication of the indicators in 2020 partly due to backlash over pro-social considerations and perceptions of widespread gaming.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The World Bank suspended the publication of the indicators in 2020, in part because of backlash about how the measures failed to adequately account for pro-social considerations and perceptions that there was widespread gaming of the system.

sections.label: Fujian gang sentencing and extradition
sections.summary: The 13 to 15 month sentences in the $3 billion Fujian gang money laundering case struck some as lenient, and the Wang Yunhe extradition raised questions about sufficiency of laws.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The sentences meted out for the $3 billion Fujian gang money laundering case of between 13 months and 15 months' jail time struck some as excessively lenient.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In a written response to the hon Member Mr Leong Mun Wai, Minister Shanmugam indicated that this duration is comparable to other jurisdictions, although he did concede that further tightening of regulatory measures was warranted.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The decision to extradite the alleged malware purveyor Wang Yunhe to the United States (US), without also prosecuting him for crimes here, also raises the question of why our laws do not appear to be sufficient to ensnare such criminal operations.

sections.label: Updated email addresses with ACRA
sections.summary: Asks the primary reasons for requiring business entities, position holders, shareholders and members to maintain updated email addresses with ACRA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What are the primary reasons for requiring business entities, position holders, shareholders and members to maintain updated email addresses with ACRA?

sections.label: Registrar obtaining Government agency information
sections.summary: A clause would empower the Registrar to obtain and use information from specified Government agencies, including email addresses and mobile numbers of company officers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: There is a clause to empower the Registrar to obtain and use information from specified Government agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Such updates should include email addresses and mobile numbers of Singaporeans and Employment Pass holders who are acting as company officers on behalf of the entities.

sections.label: Financial reporting for foreign companies
sections.summary: Asks what specific changes will streamline financial reporting requirements for foreign companies registered under the CA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What specific changes will be made to streamline financial reporting requirements for foreign companies registered under the CA?

sections.label: Tiered framework for personal data
sections.summary: Asks how the tiered framework for disclosure of personal data will ensure privacy and security for different user groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How will the tiered framework for the disclosure of personal data ensure privacy and security for different user groups?

sections.label: SME burden from new requirements
sections.summary: Asks what considerations ensure SMEs, which may lack large corporations' resources, are not disproportionately burdened by the new requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While the Bill aims to streamline regulatory processes, I would like to ask what specific considerations have been taken to ensure that SMEs, which may not have the same resources as large corporations, are not disproportionately burdened by the new requirements?

sections.label: Planned implementation timeline
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry can provide detailed insights into the planned implementation timeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide detailed insights into the planned implementation timeline?

sections.label: Data breach safeguard measures
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to elaborate on specific measures in place to safeguard data against breaches and misuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry elaborate on the specific measures that are in place to safeguard this data against breaches and misuse?

sections.label: Bill alignment with international practices
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Bill aligns with international best practices in corporate regulation and data management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How does this Bill align with international best practices in corporate regulation and data management?

sections.label: SME support and data protection
sections.summary: The passage states SMEs may need support to adapt and that the Bill must have robust data protection measures aligned with international best practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: SMEs, the backbone of our economy, may consider particular support to adapt to the new requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill must have robust data protection measures aligned with international best practices to safeguard against breaches and misuse.

sections.label: Recent money laundering cases
sections.summary: The passage states that recently there have been a series of high-profile money laundering cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, we have been recently hit by a series of high-profile money laundering cases.

sections.label: Support for Bill with concerns
sections.summary: The passage states support for the Bill while urging the Ministry to address concerns and provide a clear implementation plan with support mechanisms for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: While I support this Bill, I urge the Ministry to address these concerns and provide a clear implementation plan with support mechanisms for businesses.

sections.label: Clause 28A document effectiveness
sections.summary: The passage states Clause 28A provides that a document sent by ACRA is effective when uploaded to the recipient's digital mailbox and an email notification is sent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Clause 28A provides that the document sent by ACRA is considered effective when it is uploaded to the recipient's digital mailbox and an email notification is sent to the recipient.

sections.label: One-year digital communications transition period
sections.summary: A one-year transition period will be provided for individuals and businesses needing more time to adjust to digital communications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That said, we recognise that some individuals and businesses may need more time to adjust to digital communications.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Hence, we will provide a one-year transition period.

sections.label: Three-year period for contact addresses
sections.summary: The three-year period is to deter individuals from providing fake or unreliable contact addresses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The three-year period is to deter individuals from providing fake or unreliable contact addresses.

sections.label: Disclosure of residential addresses to lawyers
sections.summary: The disclosure framework in the Sixth Schedule may be amended to permit disclosure of residential addresses to lawyers for service of process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To provide for this, we will consider amending the disclosure framework relating to the use of personal information in the Sixth Schedule to the Bill, which can be amended as subsidiary legislation to permit disclosure of residential addresses to lawyers for the purposes of service of process.

sections.label: Breaches and Government procurement consequences
sections.summary: Breaches may lead to termination of service contracts or debarment from Government procurement, and Government agencies providing information to ACRA will be published in the Government Gazette.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Breaches may result in severe consequences, including the termination of service contracts or debarment from Government procurement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Government agencies that would provide information to ACRA will be published in the Government Gazette.

sections.label: Registrar amending register for disqualified directors
sections.summary: The Bill will empower the Registrar to amend the register based on Companies Act provisions on disqualification from acting as a director.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Bill will empower the Registrar to amend the register based on specific provisions in the Companies Act which set out the circumstances an individual is disqualified from acting as a director.

sections.label: Reducing foreign companies' administrative burden
sections.summary: The amendments aim to reduce administrative burden on foreign companies by letting them file applicable financial statements they have already prepared if Companies Act requirements are met.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The amendments aim to reduce the administrative burden on foreign companies by allowing them to file the applicable financial statements that they have already prepared as long as the requirements under the Companies Act are met.

sections.label: ACRA digital document sending
sections.summary: ACRA sends some documents only digitally; clause 28A allows hard-copy documents to be sent digitally, but residential addresses still must be filed with ACRA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Second, under existing legislation, ACRA sends certain documents only digitally, as there is no requirement for these documents to be sent in hard copy or by registered post.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For documents required by ACRA-administered legislation to be sent in hard copy, clause 28A will allow the documents to be sent digitally.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The answer is no, because the residential addresses still need to be filed with ACRA.

sections.label: Contact address delivery modes
sections.summary: A contact address is stated without requiring ordinary or prepaid registered post, unlike clause 26A, and specific documents may need specific delivery modes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: And there, it just states that a contact address, but it does not require, specifically, the language of ordinary or prepaid registered post is not included, unlike clause 26A.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I will have to have this checked specifically.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, the general principle of the contact address is that if you have done a BizFile search or a company search, you will know that when they show, let us say, director's particulars, there will always be an address.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: There will be, sometimes, when you have specific documents where you need a specific mode of delivery, for example, Court documents; or if we send reminders to pay money, we will normally do registered post.
